name: B.R.Goyal Infrastructure Ltd
title: B.R.Goyal Infrastructure Ltd - 544335 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: H1 FY27 revenue up ~61% to INR550 crore but EBITDA margin only ~6.4% and EBITDA up 28%; toll collection now half of revenue at ~50% mix, with EPC bidding strike rate just 10-15%.

summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose about 61% to INR550 crore and PAT about 38% to INR22 crore, while EBITDA grew only about 28%.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR550 crore versus INR342 crore in H1 FY26, with EPC at about INR303 crore and toll collection (TCC) at about INR236 crore. EBITA excluding other income was about INR35 crore versus INR27 crore, and PAT was about INR22 crore versus INR16 crore. Management attributed the margin gap to a lower-margin toll mix and higher petroleum-linked input costs (bitumen, diesel, cement). Order book stood at INR1,755 crore at 30 September 2026, after about INR1,087 crore of gross inflows in H1, with toll contracts forming the largest share.

segments.name: EPC (roads, buildings, wastewater)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 EPC revenue about INR303 crore. EPC order book about INR589 crore roads, INR72 crore buildings and INR132 crore wastewater, executable over 6 to 24 months. EPC strike ratio is about 10-15%.

segments.name: Toll collection contracts (TCC)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 TCC revenue about INR236 crore. TCC order book about INR962 crore; company operates about 24 toll plazas (management also cited 10 toll contracts in a separate answer). Strike ratio above 75% (management gave 70-75% and 75%).

segments.name: Wastewater and sewage
segments.commentary: Unexecuted order book about INR132 crore; management expects INR80-90 crore execution in H2 FY27 and INR300-400 crore of new orders by year end, via JVs or partnerships since the company is not yet eligible to bid solely.

segments.name: RMC (ready-mix concrete)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 1.8 lakh cubic metres per year at Indore plant (set up 2008), utilisation about 70% in H1 FY27 per analyst; management said 80-85% of capacity (90% of available operational capacity). New 1.8 lakh cubic metre plant in Indore approved by board, expected operational in H1 FY27-28.

segments.name: Residential plotting (BRG Hillview)
segments.commentary: About 1.6 lakh sq ft of plots unsold; no new customer sales booked in the current financial year as the company has paused sales.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth target of 25-30% for FY27, after FY26 turnover of INR824 crore; conservative long-term target of 20-25% annual growth.
Management expects 40-50% of toll contract order revenue to be recognised in FY27; revenue mix expected to stay about 50:50 EPC and TCC over the next 2-3 years.
PAT margin of large infra peers 8-10%; company aspires to these levels over time but not in the current year.
EPC order book expected to reach about INR1,000-1,500 crore by 31 March 2027, with EPC bidding of about INR5,000 crore planned for FY27.
Total order book expected to rise by about INR1,000-1,500 crore in FY27; management said H2 performance should be good and in line with plan.
capex_capacity: New 1.8 lakh cubic metre RMC plant in Indore approved by board; expected operational in H1 FY27-28.
Company has not set internal capital-exposure limits for toll contracts; may bid for 2-3, or about 5, toll plazas in FY27.
Exploring TOT (toll operate transfer, 20-year, upfront payment), HAM and BOT projects; no HAM/PPP bid won so far.

Working capital limit raised from INR35 crore to INR50 crore in April 2026; equipment loan enhanced by about INR10 crore; no new limits expected for 1-1.5 years unless order book reaches about INR5,000 crore.
demand_pricing: H1 FY27 gross order inflow about INR1,087 crore, including Bundelkhand Expressway toll and O&M contract from UPEIDA at INR377.54 crore for two years, and six NHAI toll plazas (about INR587 crore combined).
Escalation: government is compensating diesel and bitumen cost increases under special provisions, per management, with no profitability impact.
EBITDA margin pressure attributed to lower-margin TCC mix and higher petroleum-linked costs in EPC.
Management says EPC procurement policy changes may slow EPC awards for 1.5-2 years before a positive shift; private building opportunities being pursued in Indore (CyberCity project).

qa_highlights.question: Revenue expected from toll collection contracts in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40-50% of toll contract revenue is expected in the current financial year (FY27).

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable EBITDA margin and ROCE for toll collection versus EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: TCC needs about 5% working capital and nil plant and machinery cost; ROCE is 30-50% versus 15-25% for EPC, rising to 60-70% at scale. Contracts are one-year fixed-collection contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Why EBITDA growth (28%) lags revenue growth (61%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower blended EBITDA margin from TCC growth and higher petroleum-linked costs (bitumen, diesel, cement) in EPC.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital and bank guarantee needs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Fund-based limit is INR50 crore; total BG about INR315 crore plus cash credit; surety bonds accepted by central agencies including NHAI toll division, so no new limits expected for 1-1.5 years unless order book reaches about INR5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Wastewater expansion: organic or partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategic partnerships or JVs for now because the company lacks eligibility for direct bids in this new segment; INR300-400 crore of new orders targeted by year end.

qa_highlights.question: RMC capacity and Hillview plotting status?
qa_highlights.answer: RMC utilisation about 80-85% (90% of available capacity); new 1.8 lakh cubic metre plant planned. About 1.6 lakh sq ft of Hillview plots unsold; sales paused.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: EBITDA grew 28% against revenue growth of 61%; other expenses rose to INR392 crore from INR305 crore.
Dependence on TCC (about 50% of revenue expected): one-year contracts require re-bidding; NHAI contract renewals and bid pipeline must hold.
EPC strike ratio of 10-15% and EPC policy changes may slow awards for 1.5-2 years.
Finance cost rose after the INR15 crore working capital enhancement; watch borrowing costs as order book grows.
Cost pressure from petroleum-linked inputs; government escalation support is stated but not yet quantified.
No HAM/PPP wins to date; BOT and TOT entry depends on internal accruals and bank support.
Wastewater business has no direct eligibility; growth depends on partners.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order inflows and toll-business economics, with specific numbers on strike rates and ROCE. More cautious on near-term EBITDA, which it attributes to mix and input costs, and on EPC slowdown; it gave no quantified H2 margin guidance.
key_quotes: So, we see a good shift and a positive shift in the industry, which will happen in the coming 1.5 year to two years.
Near about our strike ratio is 10% to 15%.
Surety bonds have started being accepted by all central government agencies, and in some instances, by state agencies as well.

adds.what: New 1.8 lakh cubic metre/yr RMC plant in Indore (board approved)

growth.why: Management guides 25-30% revenue growth for FY27 (midpoint 27.5%), backed by a INR1,755 crore order book (about INR1,087 crore H1 inflows incl. UPEIDA and six NHAI toll plazas) and a board-approved 1.8 lakh cbm Indore RMC plant expected H1 FY27-28; the RMC plant is not live until about 2 quarters out and EPC award timing may slow for 1.5-2 years, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA grew about 28% vs revenue about 61% in H1 FY27 as TCC mix rose and petroleum-linked costs hit EPC; no quantified H2 margin guidance, and PAT margin is 4.02% against 8-10% aspiration that management said is not for the current year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Board approved a new 1.8 lakh cbm/yr RMC plant in Indore, matching the existing plant, with operations expected H1 FY27-28, while RMC utilisation is 80-85%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 25-30% FY27 revenue growth on a INR1,755 crore order book after about INR1,087 crore of H1 inflows, with 40-50% of toll contract revenue expected in FY27; EPC awards may slow for 1.5-2 years.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: RMC utilisation is 80-85%, and the company is exploring TOT, HAM and BOT projects and may bid for 2-3 or about 5 toll plazas in FY27, though no HAM/PPP bid has been won and funding depends on internal accruals and bank support.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management kept FY27 revenue growth at 25-30% and gave no quantified H2 margin guidance, while EBITDA lagged revenue and the EPC award pipeline may slow.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EBITDA growth of 28% trails revenue growth of 61%, other expenses rose to INR392 crore from INR305 crore, and finance costs are up after the working capital enhancement.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Wastewater is a new segment with INR132 crore unexecuted and INR300-400 crore of new orders targeted by year end, but only via JVs or partners since the company is not yet eligible to bid solely.

rows.label: Order book to INR2,755-3,255 crore by FY27 end
rows.why: Order book is INR1,755 crore and management expects a rise of INR1,000-1,500 crore in FY27 with EPC bidding about INR5,000 crore planned, though the EPC strike ratio is only 10-15%.

rows.label: Hillview plot sales resumption
rows.why: About 1.6 lakh sq ft of plots remain unsold and no new customer sales have been booked this financial year because sales are paused.

rows.label: Bank limit and BG expansion
rows.why: Fund-based limit is INR50 crore and no new limits are expected for 1-1.5 years unless the order book reaches about INR5,000 crore, against INR1,755 crore today.

tone.note: Management was confident on order inflows, toll economics (ROCE 30-50%) and strike rates, but cautious on near-term EBITDA margin due to TCC mix and petroleum costs; analysts pressed on the EBITDA-revenue gap and margin dilution.
